input.enterprise_brief_title: Meridian Health System: Seven Use Cases, Zero Decision-Grade Evidence Closures
input.enterprise_brief_summary:
Meridian Health System operates as an integrated health system and health plan anchored on Epic Hyperspace, Clarity, and Caboodle, with a fragmented on-premise analytics estate spanning SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS. An outsourced analytics managed services provider consumes an estimated 80% of delivery capacity on maintenance, leaving minimal bandwidth for net-new strategic work. AWS and Databricks represent the target platform direction — neither is production-ready, and no certified medallion architecture has been evidenced.

Ten-plus executive stakeholder groups — CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, CMO, Chief Experience Officer, Health Plan Operations, Privacy, Procurement, and the Program Office — have each confirmed seven enterprise use cases as strategic priorities: unified clinical and claims lakehouse, governed AI/LLM foundation, call center optimization, provider quality and performance, end-to-end cost transparency, payment integrity and leakage reduction, and automated close and reporting. Every use case is in planning stage. None has reached decision grade. The four pervasive blockers — no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance operating model, no certified semantic layer, and no patient/member identity spine — must be resolved before Nexus can produce sourcing-event outputs or quantified value claims. The executive decision now is: which evidence closure to fund first, and who owns accountability for each gap.
input.context_confidence_summary: Nexus has loaded 19 source-backed dimensions covering 3,987 source rows and 147 evidence references. Confidence is high on enterprise profile, system inventory, and executive use case intent. Confidence is directional on platform readiness and value hypotheses. AWS and Databricks are aspirational targets, not confirmed production foundations. All seven use cases require evidence closure before any dimension reaches decision grade.
input.evidence_gaps_summary: Four high-severity gaps block every use case simultaneously: no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance operating model, no certified semantic layer, and no patient/member identity spine. Three additional high-severity gaps are use-case-specific: provider contract terms are not digitized in governed form, transcript governance and intent taxonomy are uncertified, and SAS payment integrity model lineage is ungoverned. No realized value can be claimed until baselines and owner sign-off are in place.
input.use_cases_summary: Seven enterprise use cases are identified and source-backed: unified clinical and claims lakehouse, governed AI/LLM foundation, call center optimization, provider quality and performance, end-to-end cost transparency, payment integrity and leakage reduction, and automated close and reporting. All are in planning stage. The lakehouse and AI/LLM governance use cases are foundational prerequisites for the remaining five. No use case has cleared its evidence gate.
input.use_cases_portfolio_view: All seven use cases are in planning stage. Lakehouse and AI/LLM governance are foundational prerequisites; close their evidence gates first. Cost transparency and payment integrity can advance in parallel once governance is established. Call center optimization and provider quality follow. Automated close depends on a certified finance semantic layer and is the final sequencing step.
input.proof_summary: Nexus has assembled 147 evidence references spanning executive interviews, system records, risk and gap documentation, industry patterns, and data asset mappings. The evidence base confirms system inventory, use case intent, and a 24-item risk and gap register across all seven use cases. No evidence confirms production AI readiness, realized savings, a certified medallion architecture, or a formal data governance operating model. All value hypotheses remain planning-grade.
